relations.note: Lycaon is Callisto’s father in the dominant Arcadian genealogy.
Asius’ alternative genealogy makes Callisto the daughter of Nycteus.
Pherecydes’ alternative genealogy makes Callisto the daughter of Ceteus.
A scholion names Ceteus as Callisto’s father and Stilbe as her mother.
A scholion names Stilbe as Callisto’s mother.

relations.myth: Zeus assaults Callisto while disguised as Artemis
relations.note: Zeus assumes Artemis’ or Apollo’s form and rapes or impregnates Callisto.

relations.myth: Zeus conceals Callisto by transforming her
relations.note: One variant makes Zeus transform Callisto into a bear to conceal her.
Zeus saves Callisto from death or further danger by placing her among the stars.
Callisto bears Arcas, the Arcadian culture hero and son of Zeus.
Unaware of her identity, Arcas prepares to spear Callisto before Jupiter intervenes.
Callisto hunts with Artemis, imitates her clothing, and vows to remain a virgin.
Artemis discovers the pregnancy and expels Callisto from her company.

relations.myth: Artemis transforms Callisto into a bear
relations.note: Hesiodic and Amphis-derived variants make Artemis transform Callisto as punishment.
Artemis kills bear-shaped Callisto, either through Hera’s prompting or broken-vow anger.
Some modern reconstructions derive Callisto from Artemis Kalliste, but no ancient equation is secure.

relations.myth: Hera transforms Callisto after Arcas’ birth
relations.note: Jealous Hera transforms Callisto into a bear after she bears Arcas.

relations.myth: Hera induces Artemis to shoot Callisto
relations.note: In one variant Hera persuades Artemis to kill the bear-shaped Callisto.
At Juno’s request, Tethys prevents catasterized Callisto from entering the sea.
Juno petitions Oceanus to prevent Callisto and Arcas from setting into his waters.

relations.myth: Callisto rests beside Nomia in Hades
relations.note: Polygnotus depicted Callisto beside Nomia, with Callisto’s feet resting on her knees.

relations.myth: Callisto and Pero appear in Hades
relations.note: Polygnotus depicted Pero together with Callisto and Nomia in the Delphic underworld.
Araethus’ regional genealogy replaces Callisto with Megisto, Ceteus’ daughter and Lycaon’s granddaughter.

relations.myth: Io and Callisto displayed as parallel heroines
relations.note: Their Athenian statues were paired because both suffered animal transformation through Zeus and Hera.
